+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+"""sith - a static Python code intelligence tool.

+

+Usage:

+    python sith.py complete <file> <line> <col> [--fuzzy] [--project DIR]

+    python sith.py infer <file> <line> <col> [--project DIR]

+    python sith.py goto <file> <line> <col> [--project DIR]

+"""

+import sys

+

+from sithlib.cli import main

+

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+"""Lazily-described completion candidates.

+

+An entry stands for whatever a name refers to; its value and description are

+only computed when the name survives prefix filtering.

+"""

+from .describe import (

+    describe_class,

+    describe_function,

+    describe_module,

+    describe_param,

+    describe_value,

+)

+

+_UNSET = object()

+

+

+class BindingEntry:

+    """A name bound by a statement in parsed source."""

+

+    def __init__(self, binding, inferrer):

+        self.binding = binding

+        self.inferrer = inferrer

+

+    def value(self):

+        return self.inferrer.infer_binding(self.binding)

+

+    def describe(self, name):

+        kind = self.binding.kind

+        if kind == "param":

+            return describe_param(name)

+        if kind == "def":

+            return describe_function(name)

+        if kind == "class":

+            return describe_class(name)

+        if kind == "import":

+            return describe_module(name)

+        return describe_value(name, self.value())

+

+

+class ValueEntry:

+    """A name whose value is produced on demand by a factory."""

+

+    def __init__(self, factory):

+        self._factory = factory

+        self._value = _UNSET

+

+    def value(self):

+        if self._value is _UNSET:

+            try:

+                self._value = self._factory()

+            except Exception:

+                self._value = None

+        return self._value

+

+    def describe(self, name):

+        return describe_value(name, self.value())

+"""Static type inference: names, bindings and expressions to (unions of) values."""

+import ast

+import itertools

+import types

+import typing

+

+from .builtin_scope import builtin_entries

+from .entries import BindingEntry

+from .flow import Fact, FlowAnalyzer, initial_facts, merge

+from .members import MemberResolver

+from .scopes import CLASS, FUNCTION, LAMBDA, MODULE, Binding, walk_local

+from .values import (

+    LocalClass,

+    LocalFunction,

+    LocalInstance,

+    RuntimeClass,

+    RuntimeInstance,

+    unique,

+)

+

+_MAX_DEPTH = 60

+

+_LITERAL_TYPES = {

+    ast.JoinedStr: str,

+    ast.List: list,

+    ast.ListComp: list,

+    ast.Tuple: tuple,

+    ast.Dict: dict,

+    ast.DictComp: dict,

+    ast.Set: set,

+    ast.SetComp: set,

+    ast.GeneratorExp: types.GeneratorType,

+    ast.Compare: bool,

+}

+

+_NUMERIC_TOWER = (bool, int, float, complex)

+

+_OPERATOR_METHODS = {

+    ast.Add: "__add__", ast.Sub: "__sub__", ast.Mult: "__mul__", ast.MatMult: "__matmul__",

+    ast.Div: "__truediv__", ast.FloorDiv: "__floordiv__", ast.Mod: "__mod__",

+    ast.Pow: "__pow__", ast.LShift: "__lshift__", ast.RShift: "__rshift__",

+    ast.BitOr: "__or__", ast.BitXor: "__xor__", ast.BitAnd: "__and__",

+}

+

+NONE = RuntimeInstance(type(None))

+

+_TYPING_FORM_NAMES = ("Optional", "Union", "ClassVar", "Final", "Annotated", "Type",

+                      "Required", "NotRequired")

+_TYPING_FORMS = {id(getattr(typing, name)): name

+                 for name in _TYPING_FORM_NAMES if hasattr(typing, name)}

+

+

+def instance_of(value, init_args=None):

+    """The instance value produced by calling a class value."""

+    if isinstance(value, LocalClass):

+        return LocalInstance(value, init_args)

+    if isinstance(value, RuntimeClass):

+        return RuntimeInstance(value.obj)

+    return None

+

+

+def is_none(value):

+    return isinstance(value, RuntimeInstance) and value.cls is type(None)

+

+

+class BuiltinBinding:

+    """Stands in for a binding when a name resolves to the builtins module."""

+

+    kind = "builtin"

+

+    def __init__(self, name, entry):

+        self.name = name

+        self.entry = entry

+

+    def value(self):

+        return self.entry.value()

+

+

+class _Frame:

+    """Argument values for one call of a local function."""

+

+    _ids = itertools.count()

+

+    def __init__(self, scope, args, bound):

+        self.id = next(self._ids)

+        self.scope = scope

+        self.args = args

+        self.bound = bound

+

+

+class Inferrer:

+    def __init__(self, importer):

+        self.importer = importer

+        self.members = MemberResolver(self)

+        self._builtins = builtin_entries()

+        self._builtin_bindings = {}

+        self._binding_cache = {}

+        self._entries_cache = {}

+        self._flow_cache = {}

+        self._synthetic = {}

+        self._star_names = {}

+        self._active = set()

+        self._frames = []

+        self._depth = 0

+

+    # -- scopes and name listing (completion) -------------------------------

+

+    def scope_chain(self, scope, line, strict):

+        """(scope, line limit) pairs for name resolution starting at `scope`.

+

+        The innermost function/class scope ("local") and the module scope only

+        see bindings up to `line`.  In non-strict mode (inference inside code

+        bodies) the module scope is late-bound once a function scope was seen.

+        Class scopes are only visible from directly inside the class body.

+        """

+        chain = []

+        local_seen = False

+        for index, current in enumerate(scope.chain()):

+            if current.kind == CLASS and index > 0:

+                continue

+            if current.kind == MODULE:

+                limit = line if strict or not local_seen else None

+            elif current.kind in (FUNCTION, CLASS) and not local_seen:

+                limit = line

+                local_seen = True

+            else:

+                limit = None

+            chain.append((current, limit))

+        return chain

+

+    def scope_entries(self, scope, limit=None):

+        """Entries for names bound in `scope` (at or before line `limit`)."""

+        key = (id(scope), limit)

+        if key in self._entries_cache:

+            return self._entries_cache[key]

+        self._entries_cache[key] = {}

+        chosen = {}

+        for name, bindings in scope.bindings.items():

+            binding = _latest_binding(bindings, limit)

+            if binding is not None:

+                chosen[name] = (binding.line, BindingEntry(binding, self))

+        for star in scope.star_imports:

+            if limit is not None and star.line > limit:

+                continue

+            module = self.importer.import_module(scope.module, star.module, star.level)

+            if module is None:

+                continue

+            for name, entry in self.members.public(module).items():

+                if name not in chosen or chosen[name][0] < star.line:

+                    chosen[name] = (star.line, entry)

+        entries = {name: entry for name, (_, entry) in chosen.items()}

+        self._entries_cache[key] = entries

+        return entries

+

+    def visible_entries(self, scope, line):

+        """All names visible at `line` in `scope`, innermost definitions first."""

+        result = {}

+        for current, limit in self.scope_chain(scope, line, strict=True):

+            for name, entry in self.scope_entries(current, limit).items():

+                result.setdefault(name, entry)

+        for name, entry in self._builtins.items():

+            result.setdefault(name, entry)

+        return result

+

+    # -- flow-sensitive name resolution ------------------------------------------

+

+    def resolution_chain(self, scope, pos, strict):

+        """(scope, target position) pairs for resolving a name used at `pos` in `scope`.

+

+        Code in an enclosing scope is seen as it stands at the end of that

+        scope once a function boundary is crossed (late binding), except in

+        strict mode, which only sees what precedes the cursor.

+        """

+        chain = []

+        target = pos

+        for index, current in enumerate(scope.chain()):

+            if current.kind == CLASS and index > 0:

+                continue

+            chain.append((current, target))

+            if current.kind in (FUNCTION, LAMBDA) and not strict:

+                target = None

+        return chain

+

+    def binds(self, scope, name):

+        if name in scope.bindings:

+            return True

+        return any(self._star_binding(star, name) is not None for star in scope.star_imports)

+

+    def _star_binding(self, star, name):

+        """A synthetic binding for `name` if the star import `star` provides it."""

+        key = ("star", id(star), name)

+        if key not in self._synthetic:

+            if id(star) not in self._star_names:

+                module = self.importer.import_module(star.scope.module, star.module, star.level)

+                self._star_names[id(star)] = (

+                    set(self.members.public(module)) if module is not None else set())

+            binding = None

+            if name in self._star_names[id(star)]:

+                binding = Binding(name, star.line, "importfrom", star.node, star.scope,

+                                  extra=dict(module=star.module, level=star.level, attribute=name))

+            self._synthetic[key] = binding

+        return self._synthetic[key]

+

+    def synthetic_binding(self, scope):

+        """Factory for bindings that scope analysis does not record (see FlowAnalyzer)."""

+        stars = {id(star.node): star for star in scope.star_imports}

+

+        def create(kind, node, name):

+            if kind == "star":

+                star = stars.get(id(node))

+                return self._star_binding(star, name) if star is not None else None

+            key = (kind, id(node), name)

+            if key not in self._synthetic:

+                self._synthetic[key] = Binding(name, node.lineno, "augassign", node, scope,

+                                               target=node.target)

+            return self._synthetic[key]

+

+        return create

+

+    def flow_facts(self, scope, name, target):

+        key = (id(scope), name, target)

+        if key not in self._flow_cache:

+            analyzer = FlowAnalyzer(scope, name, target, self.synthetic_binding(scope))

+            self._flow_cache[key] = analyzer.run(initial_facts(scope, name))

+        return self._flow_cache[key]

+

+    def name_facts(self, name, scope, pos, strict=False):

+        """Facts (bindings plus narrowings) for `name` used at `pos` in `scope`."""

+        chain = self.resolution_chain(scope, pos, strict)

+        return merge(self._facts_from(name, chain, 0, ()))

+

+    def _facts_from(self, name, chain, index, narrowings):

+        for position in range(index, len(chain)):

+            current, target = chain[position]

+            if not self.binds(current, name):

+                if target is None or current.kind not in (FUNCTION, CLASS, MODULE):

+                    continue

+                # The name comes from further out, but conditions here may narrow it.

+                facts = self.flow_facts(current, name, target) or [Fact(None)]

+                result = []

+                for fact in facts:

+                    result += self._facts_from(name, chain, position + 1,

+                                               fact.narrowings + narrowings)

+                return result

+            result = []

+            for fact in self.flow_facts(current, name, target):

+                combined = fact.narrowings + narrowings

+                if fact.binding is None:

+                    result += self._facts_from(name, chain, position + 1, combined)

+                    continue

+                prior = []

+                for previous in fact.prior:

+                    if previous.binding is None:

+                        prior += self._facts_from(name, chain, position + 1, previous.narrowings)

+                    else:

+                        prior.append(previous)

+                result.append(Fact(fact.binding, combined, prior))

+            return result

+        entry = self._builtins.get(name)

+        if entry is None:

+            return []

+        if name not in self._builtin_bindings:

+            self._builtin_bindings[name] = BuiltinBinding(name, entry)

+        return [Fact(self._builtin_bindings[name], narrowings)]

+

+    def scope_facts(self, scope, name):

+        """Facts for `name` at the end of `scope` (bindings made in `scope` only)."""

+        return [f for f in self.flow_facts(scope, name, None) if f.binding is not None]

+

+    def scope_values(self, scope, name):

+        return unique(v for f in self.scope_facts(scope, name) for v in self.fact_values(f))

+

+    def name_values(self, name, scope, pos, strict=False):

+        values = []

+        for fact in self.name_facts(name, scope, pos, strict):

+            values += self.fact_values(fact)

+        return unique(values)

+

+    def fact_values(self, fact):

+        binding = fact.binding

+        if binding is None:

+            return []

+        if isinstance(binding, BuiltinBinding):

+            values = [binding.value()]

+        elif binding.kind == "augassign":

+            if fact.prior:

+                node = binding.node

+                lefts = unique(v for p in fact.prior for v in self.fact_values(p))

+                values = self._operator_values(node.op, lefts, node.value, binding.scope, None, False)

+                values = values or lefts

+            else:

+                values = self.infer_values(binding.node.value, binding.scope)

+        else:

+            values = self.binding_values(binding)

+        values = unique(values)

+        for narrowing in fact.narrowings:

+            values = self.narrow(narrowing, values)

+        return values

+

+    # -- narrowing ---------------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def narrow(self, narrowing, values):

+        if narrowing.kind == "none":

+            if narrowing.positive:

+                return [v for v in values if is_none(v)] or [NONE]

+            return [v for v in values if not is_none(v)]

+        if narrowing.kind == "truthy":

+            return [v for v in values if not is_none(v)]

+        if narrowing.kind == "isinstance":

+            classes = self.classinfo(narrowing.node, narrowing.scope)

+            if not classes:

+                return values

+            if not narrowing.positive:

+                return [v for v in values if not self.is_instance(v, classes)]

+            result = []

+            for value in values:

+                if self.is_instance(value, classes):

+                    result.append(value)

+                    continue

+                cls = self.class_of(value)

+                if cls is not None:

+                    result += [instance_of(c) for c in classes if self.is_subclass(c, cls)]

+            return unique(result) or unique(instance_of(c) for c in classes)

+        return values

+

+    def classinfo(self, node, scope):

+        elements = node.elts if isinstance(node, ast.Tuple) else [node]

+        classes = []

+        for element in elements:

+            classes += [v for v in self.infer_values(element, scope)

+                        if isinstance(v, (LocalClass, RuntimeClass))]

+        return unique(classes)

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def class_of(value):

+        if isinstance(value, LocalInstance):

+            return value.cls

+        if isinstance(value, RuntimeInstance):

+            return RuntimeClass(value.cls)

+        return None

+

+    def is_instance(self, value, classes):

+        cls = self.class_of(value)

+        return cls is not None and any(self.is_subclass(cls, c) for c in classes)

+

+    def is_subclass(self, cls, parent):

+        if isinstance(parent, RuntimeClass) and parent.obj is object:

+            return True

+        if isinstance(cls, RuntimeClass):

+            if not isinstance(parent, RuntimeClass):

+                return False

+            try:

+                return issubclass(cls.obj, parent.obj)

+            except TypeError:

+                return False

+        for current in self.members.mro(cls):

+            if isinstance(parent, LocalClass) and current.scope is parent.scope:

+                return True

+            if isinstance(parent, RuntimeClass):

+                for base in self.members.runtime_bases(current):

+                    if self.is_subclass(base, parent):

+                        return True

+        return False

+

+    # -- bindings ------------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def _frame_signature(self):

+        return tuple(frame.id for frame in self._frames)

+

+    def infer_binding(self, binding):

+        values = self.binding_values(binding)

+        return values[0] if values else None

+

+    def binding_values(self, binding):

+        key = (id(binding), self._frame_signature())

+        if key in self._binding_cache:

+            return self._binding_cache[key]

+        if key in self._active:

+            return []

+        self._active.add(key)

+        try:

+            values = unique(self._binding_values(binding))

+        except RecursionError:

+            values = []

+        finally:

+            self._active.discard(key)

+        self._binding_cache[key] = values

+        return values

+

+    def _binding_values(self, binding):

+        context = binding.scope.module

+        kind = binding.kind

+        extra = binding.extra

+        if kind == "def":

+            scope = context.scope_of(binding.node)

+            return [LocalFunction(scope)] if scope else []

+        if kind == "class":

+            scope = context.scope_of(binding.node)

+            return [LocalClass(scope)] if scope else []

+        if kind == "import":

+            return [self.importer.import_absolute(extra["module"])]

+        if kind == "importfrom":

+            return self.resolve_from_values(context, extra["module"], extra["level"],

+                                            extra["attribute"])

+        if kind == "assign":

+            annotation = extra.get("annotation")

+            if annotation is not None:

+                values = self.annotation_values(annotation, binding.scope)

+                if values:

+                    return values

+            if binding.value is not None:

+                return self.infer_values(binding.value, binding.scope)

+            return []

+        if kind == "augassign":

+            return self.infer_values(binding.node.value, binding.scope)

+        if kind == "param":

+            return self._param_values(binding)

+        if kind == "except":

+            exception = extra.get("exception")

+            if exception is None:

+                return []

+            return [instance_of(c) for c in self.classinfo(exception, binding.scope)]

+        if kind == "loop":

+            if isinstance(binding.node.target, ast.Name):

+                return self.iteration_values(binding.node.iter, binding.scope)

+            return []

+        if kind == "comprehension":

+            generator = binding.node

+            if isinstance(generator.target, ast.Name):

+                outer = binding.scope

+                if binding.scope.node.generators[0] is generator:

+                    outer = binding.scope.parent

+                return self.iteration_values(generator.iter, outer)

+            return []

+        if kind == "with":

+            for item in binding.node.items:

+                if isinstance(item.optional_vars, ast.Name) and item.optional_vars.id == binding.name:

+                    return self.enter_values(item.context_expr, binding.scope)

+            return []

+        if kind == "pattern":

+            pattern = binding.target

+            if isinstance(pattern, ast.MatchAs) and isinstance(pattern.pattern, ast.MatchClass):

+                return [instance_of(c) for c in self.classinfo(pattern.pattern.cls, binding.scope)]

+            return []

+        return []

+

+    def in_frame(self, scope, args, bound, function):

+        """Call `function()` with the parameters of `scope` bound to `args`/`bound`."""

+        self._frames.append(_Frame(scope, args, bound))

+        try:

+            return function()

+        finally:

+            self._frames.pop()

+

+    def resolve_from_values(self, context, module, level, attribute):

+        """The values imported by `from <module> import <attribute>`."""

+        if level and not module:

+            submodule = self.importer.import_relative(context, attribute, level)

+            if submodule is not None:

+                return [submodule]

+        base = self.importer.import_module(context, module, level)

+        if base is not None:

+            values = self.members.member_values(base, attribute)

+            if values:

+                return values

+        if not level and module:

+            return [self.importer.import_absolute(f"{module}.{attribute}")]

+        return []

+

+    def resolve_from(self, context, module, level, attribute):

+        values = unique(self.resolve_from_values(context, module, level, attribute))

+        return values[0] if values else None

+

+    def annotation_values(self, annotation, scope, pos=None):

+        """Instances described by a type annotation."""

+        if annotation is None:

+            return []

+        if isinstance(annotation, ast.Constant):

+            if annotation.value is None:

+                return [NONE]

+            if isinstance(annotation.value, str):

+                try:

+                    parsed = ast.parse(annotation.value.strip(), mode="eval").body

+                except SyntaxError:

+                    return []

+                return self.annotation_values(parsed, scope, pos or _position(annotation))

+            return []

+        if isinstance(annotation, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(annotation.op, ast.BitOr):

+            return unique(self.annotation_values(annotation.left, scope, pos)

+                          + self.annotation_values(annotation.right, scope, pos))

+        if isinstance(annotation, ast.Subscript):

+            arguments = annotation.slice

+            arguments = arguments.elts if isinstance(arguments, ast.Tuple) else [arguments]

+            special = _typing_form(annotation.value, self.infer_values(annotation.value, scope, pos))

+            if special == "Optional":

+                return unique(self.annotation_values(arguments[0], scope, pos) + [NONE])

+            if special == "Union":

+                return unique(v for a in arguments for v in self.annotation_values(a, scope, pos))

+            if special in ("ClassVar", "Final", "Annotated", "Required", "NotRequired"):

+                return self.annotation_values(arguments[0], scope, pos)

+            if special == "Type":

+                return [v for v in self.infer_values(arguments[0], scope, pos)

+                        if isinstance(v, (LocalClass, RuntimeClass))]

+            annotation = annotation.value

+        values = self.infer_values(annotation, scope, pos)

+        return unique(instance_of(v) for v in values if isinstance(v, (LocalClass, RuntimeClass)))

+

+    def _frame_for(self, scope):

+        for frame in reversed(self._frames):

+            if frame.scope is scope:

+                return frame

+        return None

+

+    def _param_values(self, binding):

+        node = binding.node

+        arg = binding.extra["arg"]

+        outer = binding.scope.parent

+        if arg.annotation is not None:

+            values = self.annotation_values(arg.annotation, outer)

+            if values:

+                if arg is node.args.vararg:

+                    return [RuntimeInstance(tuple)]

+                if arg is node.args.kwarg:

+                    return [RuntimeInstance(dict)]

+                return values

+        positional = node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.args

+        frame = self._frame_for(binding.scope)

+        if frame is not None:

+            if arg.arg in frame.args:

+                return frame.args[arg.arg]

+            if frame.bound is not None and positional and positional[0] is arg:

+                return [frame.bound]

+        if arg is node.args.vararg:

+            return [RuntimeInstance(tuple)]

+        if arg is node.args.kwarg:

+            return [RuntimeInstance(dict)]

+        default = _default_for(node.args, arg)

+        if default is not None:

+            return self.infer_values(default, outer)

+        is_method = isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and outer.kind == CLASS

+        if is_method and positional and positional[0] is arg:

+            decorators = {_decorator_name(d) for d in node.decorator_list}

+            if "staticmethod" in decorators:

+                return []

+            cls = LocalClass(outer)

+            if "classmethod" in decorators or node.name in ("__new__", "__init_subclass__"):

+                return [cls]

+            return [LocalInstance(cls)]

+        return []

+

+    # -- expressions -----------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def infer_values(self, node, scope, pos=None, strict=False):

+        """All values expression `node` may evaluate to in `scope`.

+

+        Names are resolved at their own position in the source, or at `pos`

+        when given (for expressions parsed separately from the module).

+        """

+        if node is None or scope is None or self._depth > _MAX_DEPTH:

+            return []

+        self._depth += 1

+        try:

+            return unique(self._infer(node, scope, pos, strict))

+        except RecursionError:

+            return []

+        finally:

+            self._depth -= 1

+

+    def _infer(self, node, scope, pos, strict):

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant):

+            return [RuntimeInstance(type(node.value))]

+        literal = _LITERAL_TYPES.get(type(node))

+        if literal is not None:

+            return [RuntimeInstance(literal)]

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Name):

+            return self.name_values(node.id, scope, pos or _position(node), strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):

+            values = []

+            for base in self.infer_values(node.value, scope, pos, strict):

+                values += self.members.member_values(base, node.attr)

+            return values

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):

+            return self._call_values(node, scope, pos, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Await):

+            if isinstance(node.value, ast.Call):

+                return self._call_values(node.value, scope, pos, strict, awaited=True)

+            return []

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Lambda):

+            lambda_scope = scope.module.scope_of(node)

+            return [LocalFunction(lambda_scope)] if lambda_scope else []

+        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):

+            return self._binop_values(node, scope, pos, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):

+            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not):

+                return [RuntimeInstance(bool)]

+            return self.infer_values(node.operand, scope, pos, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.IfExp):

+            return (self.infer_values(node.body, scope, pos, strict)

+                    + self.infer_values(node.orelse, scope, pos, strict))

+        if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):

+            return [v for value in node.values for v in self.infer_values(value, scope, pos, strict)]

+        if isinstance(node, ast.NamedExpr):

+            return self.infer_values(node.value, scope, pos, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Subscript):

+            values = self.infer_values(node.value, scope, pos, strict)

+            return [v for v in values if isinstance(v, RuntimeInstance) and v.cls in (str, bytes)]

+        return []

+

+    def _call_values(self, node, scope, pos, strict, awaited=False):

+        values = []

+        for function in self.infer_values(node.func, scope, pos, strict):

+            values += self.call_result(function, node, scope, pos, strict, awaited)

+        return values

+

+    def call_result(self, function, call, scope, pos=None, strict=False, awaited=False):

+        """Values returned by calling `function` with the arguments of `call`."""

+        if isinstance(function, LocalClass):

+            init = self.members.find_method(function, "__init__")

+            args = None

+            if init is not None:

+                args = self.map_arguments(init.node, call, scope, pos, strict, offset=1)

+            return [LocalInstance(function, args)]

+        if isinstance(function, RuntimeClass):

+            if function.obj is type and len(call.args) == 1:

+                return [c for v in self.infer_values(call.args[0], scope, pos, strict)

+                        for c in [self.class_of(v)] if c is not None]

+            return [RuntimeInstance(function.obj)]

+        if isinstance(function, LocalInstance):

+            method = self.members.find_method(function.cls, "__call__")

+            if method is None:

+                return []

+            function = LocalFunction(method.scope, function)

+        if not isinstance(function, LocalFunction):

+            return []

+        node = function.node

+        offset = 1 if function.bound is not None else 0

+        args = self.map_arguments(node, call, scope, pos, strict, offset)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef) and not awaited:

+            return [RuntimeInstance(types.CoroutineType)]

+        return self.return_values(function, args)

+

+    def map_arguments(self, function_node, call, scope, pos, strict, offset=0):

+        """{parameter name: values} for the arguments `call` passes to a function."""

+        arguments = function_node.args

+        positional = arguments.posonlyargs + arguments.args

+        mapping = {}

+        if call is None:

+            return mapping

+        for index, argument in enumerate(call.args):

+            if isinstance(argument, ast.Starred):

+                break

+            if index + offset < len(positional):

+                name = positional[index + offset].arg

+                mapping[name] = self.infer_values(argument, scope, pos, strict)

+        for keyword in call.keywords:

+            if keyword.arg is not None:

+                mapping[keyword.arg] = self.infer_values(keyword.value, scope, pos, strict)

+        return {name: values for name, values in mapping.items() if values}

+

+    def return_values(self, function, args=None):

+        """The values returned by calling a locally defined function."""

+        scope = function.scope

+        node = scope.node

+        key = ("return", id(node))

+        if key in self._active:

+            return []

+        self._active.add(key)

+        frame = _Frame(scope, args or {}, function.bound)

+        self._frames.append(frame)

+        try:

+            if isinstance(node, ast.Lambda):

+                return self.infer_values(node.body, scope)

+            if node.returns is not None:

+                values = self.annotation_values(node.returns, scope.parent)

+                if values:

+                    return values

+            returns = []

+            for child in walk_local(node.body):

+                if isinstance(child, (ast.Yield, ast.YieldFrom)):

+                    if isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef):

+                        return [RuntimeInstance(types.AsyncGeneratorType)]

+                    return [RuntimeInstance(types.GeneratorType)]

+                if isinstance(child, ast.Return):

+                    returns.append(child)

+            if not returns:

+                return [NONE]

+            values = []

+            for statement in returns:

+                if statement.value is None:

+                    values.append(NONE)

+                else:

+                    values += self.infer_values(statement.value, scope)

+            return unique(values)

+        finally:

+            self._frames.pop()

+            self._active.discard(key)

+

+    def iteration_values(self, iterable, scope):

+        """Values produced by iterating over expression `iterable`."""

+        if isinstance(iterable, (ast.List, ast.Tuple, ast.Set)):

+            return unique(v for element in iterable.elts if not isinstance(element, ast.Starred)

+                          for v in self.infer_values(element, scope))

+        if isinstance(iterable, ast.Dict):

+            return unique(v for key in iterable.keys if key is not None

+                          for v in self.infer_values(key, scope))

+        if isinstance(iterable, ast.Name):

+            literals = []

+            for fact in self.name_facts(iterable.id, scope, _position(iterable)):

+                binding = fact.binding

+                if (getattr(binding, "kind", None) == "assign" and binding.value is not None

+                        and isinstance(binding.value, (ast.List, ast.Tuple, ast.Set, ast.Dict))):

+                    literals += self.iteration_values(binding.value, binding.scope)

+            if literals:

+                return unique(literals)

+        values = []

+        for value in self.infer_values(iterable, scope):

+            if isinstance(value, RuntimeInstance):

+                if value.cls is str:

+                    values.append(value)

+                elif value.cls in (bytes, bytearray, range):

+                    values.append(RuntimeInstance(int))

+            elif isinstance(value, LocalInstance):

+                method = self.members.find_method(value.cls, "__iter__")

+                if method is not None:

+                    for iterator in self.return_values(LocalFunction(method.scope, value)):

+                        nxt = None

+                        if isinstance(iterator, LocalInstance):

+                            nxt = self.members.find_method(iterator.cls, "__next__")

+                        if nxt is not None:

+                            values += self.return_values(LocalFunction(nxt.scope, iterator))

+        return unique(values)

+

+    def enter_values(self, context_expr, scope):

+        """The value bound by `with <context_expr> as name`."""

+        values = []

+        for value in self.infer_values(context_expr, scope):

+            if isinstance(value, LocalInstance):

+                method = self.members.find_method(value.cls, "__enter__")

+                if method is not None:

+                    values += self.return_values(LocalFunction(method.scope, value))

+                    continue

+            values.append(value)

+        return unique(values)

+

+    def _binop_values(self, node, scope, pos, strict):

+        lefts = self.infer_values(node.left, scope, pos, strict)

+        return self._operator_values(node.op, lefts, node.right, scope, pos, strict)

+

+    def _operator_values(self, op, lefts, right_node, scope, pos, strict):

+        """Values of `<left> <op> <right_node>` for each of the values `lefts`."""

+        rights = None

+        values = []

+        for left in lefts:

+            if isinstance(left, LocalInstance):

+                method = self.members.find_method(left.cls, _OPERATOR_METHODS.get(type(op), ""))

+                if method is not None:

+                    values += self.return_values(LocalFunction(method.scope, left))

+                continue

+            if not isinstance(left, RuntimeInstance):

+                continue

+            if isinstance(op, ast.Mod) and left.cls in (str, bytes):

+                values.append(left)

+                continue

+            if rights is None:

+                rights = self.infer_values(right_node, scope, pos, strict)

+            for right in rights:

+                if not isinstance(right, RuntimeInstance):

+                    continue

+                if right.cls is left.cls:

+                    if left.cls is bool and not isinstance(op, (ast.BitAnd, ast.BitOr, ast.BitXor)):

+                        values.append(RuntimeInstance(int))

+                    elif left.cls is int and isinstance(op, ast.Div):

+                        values.append(RuntimeInstance(float))

+                    else:

+                        values.append(left)

+                elif left.cls in _NUMERIC_TOWER and right.cls in _NUMERIC_TOWER:

+                    wider = max(left.cls, right.cls, key=_NUMERIC_TOWER.index)

+                    values.append(RuntimeInstance(max(wider, int, key=_NUMERIC_TOWER.index)))

+                elif isinstance(op, ast.Mult) and {left.cls, right.cls} & {int, bool}:

+                    sequence = right.cls if left.cls in (int, bool) else left.cls

+                    values.append(RuntimeInstance(sequence))

+        return values

+

+

+def _position(node):

+    return (node.lineno, node.col_offset)

+

+

+def _typing_form(node, values):

+    """The name of a typing special form (Optional, Union, ...) used as `node`."""

+    for value in values:

+        obj = getattr(value, "obj", None)

+        if obj is not None and id(obj) in _TYPING_FORMS:

+            return _TYPING_FORMS[id(obj)]

+        if isinstance(value, RuntimeClass) and value.obj is type:

+            return "Type"

+    name = node.attr if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) else getattr(node, "id", None)

+    if not values and name in _TYPING_FORM_NAMES:

+        return name

+    return None

+

+

+def _latest_binding(bindings, limit):

+    """The binding in effect at line `limit` (any line when `limit` is None).

+

+    A binding on the limit line itself (e.g. `x = x + 1`, or the statement

+    being typed) only counts when there is no earlier one.

+    """

+    if limit is None:

+        pool = bindings

+    else:

+        pool = [b for b in bindings if b.line < limit] or [b for b in bindings if b.line == limit]

+    if not pool:

+        return None

+    return max(enumerate(pool), key=lambda pair: (pair[1].line, pair[0]))[1]

+

+

+def _default_for(arguments, arg):

+    positional = arguments.posonlyargs + arguments.args

+    if arg in positional:

+        offset = len(positional) - len(arguments.defaults)

+        index = positional.index(arg)

+        return arguments.defaults[index - offset] if index >= offset else None

+    if arg in arguments.kwonlyargs:

+        return arguments.kw_defaults[arguments.kwonlyargs.index(arg)]

+    return None

+

+

+def _decorator_name(node):

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):

+        node = node.func

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):

+        return node.attr

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):

+        return node.id

+    return None

+

+"""The completion engine: ties context, parsing, scopes and inference together."""

+import ast

+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

+

+from . import context as cursor_context

+from .builtin_scope import KEYWORDS

+from .describe import describe_keyword

+from .inference import Inferrer

+from .locate import find_scope

+from .matching import make_matcher

+from .members import is_public

+from .modules import Importer, ModuleContext

+from .parsing import parse_tolerant

+from .ranking import sort_keywords, sort_names

+from .source import load_document

+from .values import MODULE

+

+

+@dataclass

+class Completion:

+    name: str

+    complete: str

+    type: str

+    description: str

+

+    def to_dict(self):

+        return asdict(self)

+

+

+def complete_file(path, line, col, fuzzy=False, project=None):

+    """Completions for the cursor at 1-based `line`, 0-based `col` of `path`."""

+    document = load_document(path)

+    document.check_position(line, col)

+    return Completer(document, line, col, fuzzy, project).run()

+

+

+class Completer:

+    def __init__(self, document, line, col, fuzzy, project=None):

+        self.document = document

+        self.line = line

+        self.col = col

+        self.fuzzy = fuzzy

+        self.project = project

+

+    def run(self):

+        request = cursor_context.analyze(self.document.text_before(self.line, self.col))

+        if request.kind == cursor_context.NONE:

+            return []

+

+        importer = Importer(self.project or self.document.directory, self.document.directory)

+        tree = parse_tolerant(self.document.text, cursor=(self.line, self.col))

+        module = ModuleContext(self.document.path, "__main__", tree, self.document.text)

+        importer.register(module)

+        inferrer = Inferrer(importer)

+        scope = find_scope(module, self.line, self.col, self.document.lines[self.line - 1])

+

+        if request.kind == cursor_context.ATTRIBUTE:

+            entries = self._attribute_entries(inferrer, scope, request.receiver)

+            keywords = []

+        else:

+            entries = inferrer.visible_entries(scope, self.line)

+            keywords = KEYWORDS

+

+        matches = make_matcher(request.prefix, self.fuzzy)

+        cut = len(request.prefix)

+        results = []

+        for name in sort_names(n for n in entries if matches(n)):

+            kind, description = entries[name].describe(name)

+            results.append(Completion(name, name[cut:], kind, description))

+        for name in sort_keywords(k for k in keywords if matches(k)):

+            kind, description = describe_keyword(name)

+            results.append(Completion(name, name[cut:], kind, description))

+        return results

+

+    def _attribute_entries(self, inferrer, scope, receiver):

+        try:

+            expression = ast.parse(receiver.strip(), mode="eval").body

+        except (SyntaxError, ValueError):

+            return {}

+        line_text = self.document.lines[self.line - 1]

+        position = (self.line, len(line_text[:self.col].encode("utf-8")))

+        entries = {}

+        for value in inferrer.infer_values(expression, scope, pos=position, strict=True):

+            members = inferrer.members.all(value)

+            if value.kind == MODULE:

+                members = {name: entry for name, entry in members.items() if is_public(name)}

+            for name, entry in members.items():

+                entries.setdefault(name, entry)

+        return entries

+    column: int

+    docstring: str

+        return (self.module_path, self.line, self.column)

+def sorted_unique(definitions):

+        if identity not in seen:

+            seen.add(identity)

+            result.append(definition)

+    match = re.compile(r"(?<![\w])" + re.escape(word) + r"(?![\w])").search(text, max(start, 0))

+    path = ""

+"""Command-line interface: argument parsing, JSON output and exit codes."""

+import argparse

+import contextlib

+import io

+import json

+import sys

+

+from .completion import complete_file

+from .errors import SithError

+from .navigation import GOTO, INFER, navigate

+

+

+class _ArgumentParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):

+    """An ArgumentParser that reports usage errors as SithError (exit 1)."""

+

+    def error(self, message):

+        raise SithError(message)

+

+

+def _add_position_arguments(parser):

+    parser.add_argument("file", help="Python source file")

+    parser.add_argument("line", type=int, help="1-based line number")

+    parser.add_argument("col", type=int, help="0-based column number")

+    parser.add_argument("--project", default=None,

+                        help="project root (default: the directory containing the file)")

+

+

+def build_parser():

+    parser = _ArgumentParser(prog="sith.py", description="Python code intelligence.")

+    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True, parser_class=_ArgumentParser)

+    complete = commands.add_parser("complete", help="complete the code at a cursor position")

+    _add_position_arguments(complete)

+    complete.add_argument("--fuzzy", action="store_true", help="use fuzzy matching")

+    infer = commands.add_parser(INFER, help="infer what the name at a cursor position evaluates to")

+    _add_position_arguments(infer)

+    goto = commands.add_parser(GOTO, help="find where the name at a cursor position is defined")

+    _add_position_arguments(goto)

+    return parser

+

+

+def _run(args):

+    if args.command == "complete":

+        completions = complete_file(args.file, args.line, args.col, fuzzy=args.fuzzy,

+                                    project=args.project)

+        return "completions", [c.to_dict() for c in completions]

+    definitions = navigate(args.command, args.file, args.line, args.col, project=args.project)

+    return "definitions", [d.to_dict() for d in definitions]

+

+

+def main(argv=None):

+    key = "completions"

+    try:

+        args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)

+        key = "completions" if args.command == "complete" else "definitions"

+        # Introspected modules may print; keep STDOUT reserved for the JSON result.

+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):

+            key, results = _run(args)

+    except SithError as error:

+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)

+        return 1

+    except Exception as error:  # analysis must never crash an editor integration

+        print(f"warning: analysis failed: {error!r}", file=sys.stderr)

+        results = []

+    payload = {key: results}

+    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")

+    return 0

+"""Textual analysis of the cursor position: prefix and completion kind."""

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+

+NAME = "name"

+ATTRIBUTE = "attribute"

+NONE = "none"

+

+_OPENERS = {")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{"}

+_STRING_PREFIX_CHARS = "rRbBuUfF"

+

+

+@dataclass

+class CursorContext:

+    """What kind of completion is requested and what has been typed so far."""

+

+    kind: str

+    prefix: str = ""

+    receiver: str = ""

+

+

+def is_identifier_char(char):

+    return char == "_" or char.isalnum()

+

+

+def analyze(text_before_cursor):

+    """Classify the completion request from the source text before the cursor."""

+    end = len(text_before_cursor)

+    start = end

+    while start > 0 and is_identifier_char(text_before_cursor[start - 1]):

+        start -= 1

+    prefix = text_before_cursor[start:]

+    if prefix and prefix[0].isdigit():

+        return CursorContext(NONE, prefix)

+

+    before = text_before_cursor[:start]

+    if not before.endswith("."):

+        return CursorContext(NAME, prefix)

+

+    receiver = extract_receiver(before[:-1])

+    if not receiver or receiver.isdigit() or receiver.endswith("."):

+        return CursorContext(NONE, prefix)

+    return CursorContext(ATTRIBUTE, prefix, receiver)

+

+

+def extract_receiver(text):

+    """Return the expression text that ends at the end of `text`, or None."""

+    i = len(text)

+    while i > 0:

+        char = text[i - 1]

+        if char in _OPENERS:

+            opener = _match_open(text, i - 1)

+            if opener is None:

+                return None

+            i = opener

+            continue

+        if is_identifier_char(char):

+            while i > 0 and is_identifier_char(text[i - 1]):

+                i -= 1

+            if i > 0 and text[i - 1] == ".":

+                i -= 1

+                continue

+            break

+        if char in "\"'":

+            start = _string_start(text, i - 1)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            i = start

+            while i > 0 and text[i - 1] in _STRING_PREFIX_CHARS:

+                i -= 1

+            break

+        break

+    return text[i:].strip()

+

+

+def _match_open(text, close_index):

+    """Index of the bracket opening the one at `close_index`, scanning backwards."""

+    stack = [text[close_index]]

+    i = close_index - 1

+    while i >= 0:

+        char = text[i]

+        if char in "\"'":

+            start = _string_start(text, i)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            i = start - 1

+            continue

+        if char in _OPENERS:

+            stack.append(char)

+        elif char in "([{":

+            if _OPENERS[stack[-1]] != char:

+                return None

+            stack.pop()

+            if not stack:

+                return i

+        i -= 1

+    return None

+

+

+def _string_start(text, end_index):

+    """Index of the opening quote of the string literal ending at `end_index`."""

+    quote = text[end_index]

+    if end_index >= 2 and text[end_index - 2:end_index + 1] == quote * 3:

+        start = text.rfind(quote * 3, 0, end_index - 2)

+        return None if start < 0 else start

+    i = end_index - 1

+    while i >= 0:

+        if text[i] == quote and (i == 0 or text[i - 1] != "\\"):

+            return i

+        if text[i] == "\n":

+            return None

+        i -= 1

+    return None

+"""Loading source documents and validating cursor positions."""

+import os

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+

+from .errors import SithError

+

+

+@dataclass

+class Document:

+    """A source file split into lines, with cursor-related helpers."""

+

+    path: str

+    text: str

+    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)

+

+    @property

+    def directory(self):

+        return os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))

+

+    def check_position(self, line, col):

+        """Validate a 1-based line and 0-based column."""

+        if line < 1 or line > len(self.lines):

+            raise SithError(f"line {line} is out of range (file has {len(self.lines)} lines)")

+        length = len(self.lines[line - 1])

+        if col < 0 or col > length:

+            raise SithError(f"column {col} is out of range (line {line} has {length} characters)")

+

+    def text_before(self, line, col):

+        """All source text preceding the cursor."""

+        return "\n".join(self.lines[: line - 1] + [self.lines[line - 1][:col]])

+

+

+def normalize_newlines(text):

+    return text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

+

+

+def read_text(path):

+    """Read a file as UTF-8 text, raising SithError on any problem."""

+    if not os.path.exists(path):

+        raise SithError(f"file not found: {path}")

+    if not os.path.isfile(path):

+        raise SithError(f"not a regular file: {path}")

+    try:

+        with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+            raw = handle.read()

+    except OSError as exc:

+        raise SithError(f"cannot read {path}: {exc}") from exc

+    try:

+        text = raw.decode("utf-8")

+    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:

+        raise SithError(f"file is not valid UTF-8: {path}") from exc

+    if text.startswith("\ufeff"):

+        text = text[1:]

+    return normalize_newlines(text)

+

+

+def load_document(path):

+    text = read_text(path)

+    return Document(path=path, text=text, lines=text.split("\n"))

+"""Flow-sensitive name resolution within a single scope.

+

+For one name in one scope, the analyzer walks the scope's statements in

+execution order and tracks which bindings may be in effect, as a list of

+facts.  Branches (`if`, loops, `try`, `match`) merge the facts of every path;

+`return`, `raise`, `break` and `continue` end a path.  Conditions such as

+`isinstance(x, A)` or `x is None` attach narrowings to the facts of the

+branches they guard.  Values are only inferred later, from the facts.

+"""

+import ast

+

+from .scopes import COMPREHENSION, FUNCTION, LAMBDA, walk_local

+

+_COMPOUND = (ast.If, ast.For, ast.AsyncFor, ast.While, ast.With, ast.AsyncWith, ast.Try, ast.Match)

+if hasattr(ast, "TryStar"):

+    _COMPOUND += (ast.TryStar,)

+# Nodes whose children are not evaluated as part of the enclosing statement's header.

+_NOT_HEADER = (ast.stmt, ast.Lambda, ast.excepthandler, ast.match_case)

+

+

+class Narrowing:

+    """A condition known to hold (`positive`) or not for a name at some point.

+

+    Kinds: "isinstance" (`node` is the class expression, evaluated in

+    `scope`), "none" (`x is None`) and "truthy" (`if x:`).

+    """

+

+    def __init__(self, kind, positive, node=None, scope=None):

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.positive = positive

+        self.node = node

+        self.scope = scope

+

+    @property

+    def key(self):

+        return (self.kind, self.positive, id(self.node))

+

+

+class Fact:

+    """One way a name may be bound at a program point.

+

+    `binding` is None when the name refers to an enclosing scope (or is not

+    yet bound here).  `prior` holds the facts an augmented assignment updates.

+    """

+

+    def __init__(self, binding, narrowings=(), prior=()):

+        self.binding = binding

+        self.narrowings = tuple(narrowings)

+        self.prior = tuple(prior)

+

+    @property

+    def key(self):

+        return (id(self.binding), tuple(n.key for n in self.narrowings),

+                tuple(p.key for p in self.prior))

+

+    def narrowed(self, narrowing):

+        return Fact(self.binding, self.narrowings + (narrowing,), self.prior)

+

+

+def merge(*states):

+    """The union of several lists of facts, without duplicates."""

+    seen = set()

+    result = []

+    for state in states:

+        for fact in state:

+            if fact.key not in seen:

+                seen.add(fact.key)

+                result.append(fact)

+    return result

+

+

+def start_of(node):

+    return (node.lineno, node.col_offset)

+

+

+def end_of(node):

+    return (node.end_lineno, node.end_col_offset)

+

+

+class _Found(Exception):

+    def __init__(self, state):

+        super().__init__()

+        self.state = state

+

+

+class _Loop:

+    def __init__(self):

+        self.breaks = []

+        self.continues = []

+

+

+class FlowAnalyzer:

+    """Computes the facts for `name` in `scope` at `target` ((line, byte col) or None for the end).

+

+    `synthetic(kind, node, name)` creates bindings that scope analysis does

+    not record: "star" for `from m import *` and "aug" for `x += ...`.

+    """

+

+    def __init__(self, scope, name, target, synthetic):

+        self.scope = scope

+        self.name = name

+        self.target = target

+        self.synthetic = synthetic

+        self.searching = target is not None

+        self.by_node = {}

+        self.seen = set()

+        self.loops = []

+        for binding in scope.bindings.get(name, []):

+            self.by_node.setdefault(id(binding.node), []).append(binding)

+        self.has_walrus = any(isinstance(b.node, ast.NamedExpr) for b in scope.bindings.get(name, []))

+

+    def run(self, initial):

+        bindings = self.scope.bindings.get(self.name, [])

+        if self.scope.kind in (LAMBDA, COMPREHENSION):

+            return [Fact(b) for b in bindings] or list(initial)

+        body = self.scope.node.body

+        # Bindings made elsewhere, by functions declaring the name `global`.

+        local = self.scope.local_node_ids

+        if local is None:

+            local = self.scope.local_node_ids = {id(node) for node in walk_local(body)}

+        foreign = [Fact(b) for b in bindings if b.kind != "param" and id(b.node) not in local]

+        try:

+            state = self.block(body, list(initial))

+        except _Found as found:

+            state = found.state

+            if not state or all(fact.binding is None for fact in state):

+                return state

+        return merge(state, foreign)

+

+    # -- statements ----------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def block(self, statements, state):

+        for statement in statements:

+            if self.searching:

+                if self.target < start_of(statement):

+                    raise _Found(state)

+                if self.target <= end_of(statement):

+                    self._enter(statement, state)

+            state = self.statement(statement, state)

+        return state

+

+    def _enter(self, statement, state):

+        """The target lies within `statement`: find the facts that reach it."""

+        first = _first_child_start(statement)

+        if first is None or self.target < first:

+            raise _Found(state)

+        raise _Found(self.statement(statement, state))

+

+    def statement(self, node, state):

+        handler = getattr(self, "_" + type(node).__name__, None)

+        if handler is not None:

+            return handler(node, state)

+        return self._bind(node, self.walrus(node, state))

+

+    def _bind(self, node, state):

+        """The state after `node` binds the name (unchanged if it does not)."""

+        bindings = self.by_node.get(id(node))

+        if not bindings:

+            return state

+        for binding in bindings:

+            self.seen.add(id(binding))

+        return [Fact(bindings[-1])]

+

+    def walrus(self, node, state):

+        """Apply `(name := value)` bindings found in the header expressions of `node`."""

+        if not self.has_walrus:

+            return state

+        stack = [c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(node) if not isinstance(c, _NOT_HEADER)]

+        if isinstance(node, ast.expr):

+            stack = [node]

+        while stack:

+            child = stack.pop()

+            if isinstance(child, ast.NamedExpr):

+                state = self._bind(child, state)

+            stack.extend(c for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(child) if not isinstance(c, _NOT_HEADER))

+        return state

+

+    def _ImportFrom(self, node, state):

+        if any(alias.name == "*" for alias in node.names):

+            binding = self.synthetic("star", node, self.name)

+            return [Fact(binding)] if binding is not None else state

+        return self._bind(node, state)

+

+    def _AugAssign(self, node, state):

+        state = self.walrus(node.value, state)

+        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name) and node.target.id == self.name:

+            bindings = self.by_node.get(id(node))

+            binding = bindings[-1] if bindings else self.synthetic("aug", node, self.name)

+            self.seen.add(id(binding))

+            return [Fact(binding, prior=state)]

+        return state

+

+    def _Delete(self, node, state):

+        for target in node.targets:

+            if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == self.name:

+                return []

+        return state

+

+    def _Return(self, node, state):

+        self.walrus(node, state)

+        return []

+

+    _Raise = _Return

+

+    def _Break(self, node, state):

+        if self.loops:

+            self.loops[-1].breaks.extend(state)

+        return []

+

+    def _Continue(self, node, state):

+        if self.loops:

+            self.loops[-1].continues.extend(state)

+        return []

+

+    def _Assert(self, node, state):

+        return self.branch(node.test, self.walrus(node, state), True)

+

+    def _If(self, node, state):

+        state = self.walrus(node.test, state)

+        body = self.block(node.body, self.branch(node.test, state, True))

+        orelse = self.block(node.orelse, self.branch(node.test, state, False))

+        return merge(body, orelse)

+

+    def _loop(self, node, state, enter):

+        """(state when the loop ends normally, states at `break`)."""

+        searching = self.searching

+        self.searching = False

+        self.loops.append(_Loop())

+        try:

+            first = self.block(node.body, enter(state))

+        finally:

+            loop = self.loops.pop()

+            self.searching = searching

+        start = merge(state, first, loop.continues)

+        self.loops.append(_Loop())

+        try:

+            end = self.block(node.body, enter(start))

+        finally:

+            loop = self.loops.pop()

+        return merge(start, end, loop.continues), loop.breaks

+

+    def _While(self, node, state):

+        state = self.walrus(node.test, state)

+        exit_state, breaks = self._loop(node, state, lambda s: self.branch(node.test, s, True))

+        if isinstance(node.test, ast.Constant) and node.test.value:

+            exit_state = []

+        else:

+            exit_state = self.branch(node.test, exit_state, False)

+        return merge(self.block(node.orelse, exit_state), breaks)

+

+    def _For(self, node, state):

+        state = self.walrus(node.iter, state)

+        bindings = self.by_node.get(id(node))

+        if bindings:

+            for binding in bindings:

+                self.seen.add(id(binding))

+            enter = lambda s: [Fact(bindings[-1])]

+        else:

+            enter = lambda s: s

+        exit_state, breaks = self._loop(node, state, enter)

+        return merge(self.block(node.orelse, exit_state), breaks)

+

+    _AsyncFor = _For

+

+    def _With(self, node, state):

+        for item in node.items:

+            state = self.walrus(item.context_expr, state)

+        return self.block(node.body, self._bind(node, state))

+

+    _AsyncWith = _With

+

+    def _Try(self, node, state):

+        body = self.block(node.body, state)

+        handler_start = merge(state, body)

+        ends = [self.block(node.orelse, body)]

+        for handler in node.handlers:

+            ends.append(self.block(handler.body, self._bind(handler, handler_start)))

+        result = merge(*ends)

+        if not node.finalbody:

+            return result

+        after = self.block(node.finalbody, merge(result, handler_start))

+        return after if result else []

+

+    _TryStar = _Try

+

+    def _Match(self, node, state):

+        state = self.walrus(node.subject, state)

+        ends = [state]

+        for case in node.cases:

+            ends.append(self.block(case.body, self._bind(case, state)))

+        return merge(*ends)

+

+    # -- conditions ------------------------------------------------------------

+

+    def branch(self, test, state, positive):

+        """The facts in the branch where `test` is true (`positive`) or false."""

+        if not state:

+            return state

+        if isinstance(test, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(test.op, ast.Not):

+            return self.branch(test.operand, state, not positive)

+        if isinstance(test, ast.BoolOp):

+            if isinstance(test.op, ast.And) == positive:

+                for value in test.values:

+                    state = self.branch(value, state, positive)

+                return state

+            result = []

+            for value in test.values:

+                result = merge(result, self.branch(value, state, positive))

+                state = self.branch(value, state, not positive)

+            return result

+        narrowing = self._narrowing(test, positive)

+        if narrowing is None:

+            return state

+        return [fact.narrowed(narrowing) for fact in state]

+

+    def _is_subject(self, node):

+        if isinstance(node, ast.NamedExpr):

+            node = node.target

+        return isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == self.name

+

+    def _narrowing(self, test, positive):

+        if self._is_subject(test):

+            return Narrowing("truthy", True) if positive else None

+        if isinstance(test, ast.Call) and isinstance(test.func, ast.Name) and len(test.args) == 2:

+            if test.func.id == "isinstance" and self._is_subject(test.args[0]):

+                return Narrowing("isinstance", positive, test.args[1], self.scope)

+            return None

+        if isinstance(test, ast.Compare) and len(test.ops) == 1:

+            left, op, right = test.left, test.ops[0], test.comparators[0]

+            if _is_none(left) and self._is_subject(right):

+                left, right = right, left

+            if self._is_subject(left) and _is_none(right):

+                if isinstance(op, (ast.Is, ast.Eq)):

+                    return Narrowing("none", positive)

+                if isinstance(op, (ast.IsNot, ast.NotEq)):

+                    return Narrowing("none", not positive)

+            if (positive and isinstance(op, (ast.Is, ast.Eq)) and isinstance(left, ast.Call)

+                    and isinstance(left.func, ast.Name) and left.func.id == "type"

+                    and len(left.args) == 1 and self._is_subject(left.args[0])):

+                return Narrowing("isinstance", True, right, self.scope)

+        return None

+

+

+def _is_none(node):

+    return isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and node.value is None

+

+

+def _first_child_start(statement):

+    """Start of the first nested statement (or case) of a compound statement."""

+    if not isinstance(statement, _COMPOUND):

+        return None

+    if isinstance(statement, ast.Match):

+        return start_of(statement.cases[0].pattern) if statement.cases else None

+    return start_of(statement.body[0]) if statement.body else None

+

+

+def initial_facts(scope, name):

+    """Facts at the start of `scope`: its parameter binding, or the enclosing scope."""

+    if scope.kind == FUNCTION:

+        params = [b for b in scope.bindings.get(name, []) if b.kind == "param"]

+        if params:

+            return [Fact(params[-1])]

+    return [Fact(None)]

+"""Module contexts and import resolution (local files first, then installed)."""

+import contextlib

+import importlib

+import io

+import os

+import warnings

+

+from .parsing import parse_tolerant

+from .scopes import ScopeBuilder

+from .source import read_text

+from .errors import SithError

+from .values import LocalModule, RuntimeModule

+

+

+class ModuleContext:

+    """A parsed Python module together with its scope tree."""

+

+    def __init__(self, path, name, tree, text=""):

+        self.path = os.path.abspath(path) if path else None

+        self.directory = os.path.dirname(self.path) if self.path else os.getcwd()

+        self.name = name

+        self.tree = tree

+        self.text = text

+        self.lines = text.split("\n")

+        builder = ScopeBuilder(self)

+        self.root = builder.build(tree)

+        self.scope_by_node = builder.scope_by_node

+        self.binding_by_target = builder.binding_by_target

+

+    @property

+    def is_package(self):

+        return bool(self.path) and os.path.basename(self.path) == "__init__.py"

+

+    def scope_of(self, node):

+        return self.scope_by_node.get(id(node))

+

+    def binding_of(self, node):

+        """The binding created for a name node (or def/class/except node), if any."""

+        return self.binding_by_target.get(id(node))

+

+

+class Importer:

+    """Resolves module names to values, preferring files in the project directory."""

+

+    def __init__(self, project_dir, *extra_dirs):

+        self.project_dir = project_dir

+        self.search_dirs = [project_dir] + [d for d in extra_dirs if d and d != project_dir]

+        self._contexts = {}

+        self._runtime = {}

+

+    def register(self, context):

+        if context.path:

+            self._contexts[context.path] = context

+

+    def context_for_file(self, path, name):

+        path = os.path.abspath(path)

+        if path not in self._contexts:

+            try:

+                text = read_text(path)

+            except SithError:

+                return None

+            self._contexts[path] = ModuleContext(path, name, parse_tolerant(text), text)

+        return self._contexts[path]

+

+    def import_absolute(self, dotted):

+        """Resolve `import dotted` to a module value, or None."""

+        if not dotted:

+            return None

+        path = None

+        for directory in self.search_dirs:

+            path = self._find_local(directory, dotted.split("."))

+            if path:

+                break

+        if path:

+            context = self.context_for_file(path, dotted)

+            return LocalModule(context) if context else None

+        return self._import_runtime(dotted)

+

+    def import_relative(self, context, dotted, level):

+        """Resolve `from <level dots><dotted> import ...` relative to `context`."""

+        base = context.directory

+        for _ in range(level - 1):

+            base = os.path.dirname(base)

+        parts = dotted.split(".") if dotted else []

+        path = self._find_local(base, parts) if parts else _package_init(base)

+        if not path:

+            return None

+        name = ".".join(p for p in [os.path.basename(base)] + parts if p)

+        context = self.context_for_file(path, name)

+        return LocalModule(context) if context else None

+

+    def import_module(self, context, dotted, level=0):

+        if level:

+            return self.import_relative(context, dotted, level)

+        return self.import_absolute(dotted)

+

+    def local_submodule(self, module_value, name):

+        """A submodule `name` of a local package, if such a file exists."""

+        context = module_value.context

+        if not context.is_package:

+            return None

+        path = self._find_local(context.directory, [name])

+        if not path:

+            return None

+        sub = self.context_for_file(path, f"{context.name}.{name}")

+        return LocalModule(sub) if sub else None

+

+    def runtime_submodule(self, module_value, name):

+        if not hasattr(module_value.obj, "__path__"):

+            return None

+        return self._import_runtime(f"{module_value.obj.__name__}.{name}")

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def _find_local(base, parts):

+        directory = base

+        for part in parts[:-1]:

+            directory = os.path.join(directory, part)

+            if not os.path.isdir(directory):

+                return None

+        last = os.path.join(directory, parts[-1])

+        if os.path.isfile(last + ".py"):

+            return last + ".py"

+        return _package_init(last)

+

+    def _import_runtime(self, dotted):

+        if dotted not in self._runtime:

+            module = None

+            try:

+                with warnings.catch_warnings(), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):

+                    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

+                    module = importlib.import_module(dotted)

+            except BaseException:  # importing arbitrary modules may fail in any way

+                module = None

+            self._runtime[dotted] = RuntimeModule(module) if module is not None else None

+        return self._runtime[dotted]

+

+

+def _package_init(directory):

+    init = os.path.join(directory, "__init__.py")

+    return init if os.path.isfile(init) else None

+            else:

+        if candidate is None:

+        if not inside:

+

+def _contains(node, line, byte_col):

+    start = (node.lineno, node.col_offset)

+    end = (node.end_lineno, node.end_col_offset)

+    return start <= (line, byte_col) <= end

+

+def _innermost_expression_scope(scope, line, byte_col):

+    """Descend into lambda/comprehension scopes that contain the cursor."""

+    while True:

+        for child in scope.children:

+            if child.kind in (LAMBDA, COMPREHENSION) and _contains(child.node, line, byte_col):

+                scope = child

+                break

+        else:

+            return scope

+"""Scope analysis: which names each scope binds, and where."""

+import ast

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+from .parsing import PLACEHOLDER

+MODULE = "module"

+FUNCTION = "function"

+CLASS = "class"

+LAMBDA = "lambda"

+COMPREHENSION = "comprehension"

+

+_FUNCTION_NODES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)

+_COMPREHENSION_NODES = (ast.ListComp, ast.SetComp, ast.DictComp, ast.GeneratorExp)

+

+@dataclass(eq=False)

+class Binding:

+    """A single place where a name is bound."""

+

+    name: str

+    line: int

+    kind: str

+    node: ast.AST

+    scope: "Scope"

+    value: ast.AST = None

+    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

+    # The node naming the bound identifier (ast.Name, ast.arg, ast.alias, ...).

+    target: ast.AST = None

+

+

+@dataclass(eq=False)

+class StarImport:

+    """A `from module import *` statement."""

+

+    module: str

+    level: int

+    line: int

+    scope: "Scope"

+    node: ast.AST = None

+class Scope:

+    """A namespace: module, function, class, lambda or comprehension."""

+

+    def __init__(self, kind, node, parent, module):

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.node = node

+        self.parent = parent

+        self.module = module

+        self.bindings = {}

+        self.star_imports = []

+        self.children = []

+        self.global_names = set()

+        self.local_node_ids = None  # ids of the nodes of the body, cached by flow analysis

+        self.bindings.setdefault(binding.name, []).append(binding)

+

+    def chain(self):

+        scope = self

+        while scope is not None:

+            yield scope

+            scope = scope.parent

+

+    def root(self):

+        scope = self

+        while scope.parent is not None:

+            scope = scope.parent

+        return scope

+

+

+def iter_target_names(target, value):

+    """Yield (Name node, value expression or None) pairs for an assignment target."""

+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):

+        self._statements(scope, node.orelse)

+    _stmt_AsyncFor = _stmt_For

+

+    def _stmt_With(self, scope, node):

+        for item in node.items:

+            self._expression(scope, item.context_expr)

+            if item.optional_vars is not None:

+                self._bind_target(scope, item.optional_vars, "with", None, node,

+                                  context=item.context_expr)

+        self._statements(scope, node.body)

+

+    _stmt_AsyncWith = _stmt_With

+

+    def _stmt_Try(self, scope, node):

+        self._statements(scope, node.body)

+        for handler in node.handlers:

+            self._expression(scope, handler.type)

+            if handler.name:

+                self._bind(scope, handler.name, handler.lineno, "except", handler,

+                           exception=handler.type)

+            self._statements(scope, handler.body)

+        self._statements(scope, node.finalbody)

+    _stmt_TryStar = _stmt_Try

+    def _stmt_Match(self, scope, node):

+        self._expression(scope, node.subject)

+            for pattern in ast.walk(case.pattern):

+                for attribute in ("name", "rest"):

+                    name = getattr(pattern, attribute, None)

+                    if isinstance(name, str):

+                        self._bind(scope, name, pattern.lineno, "pattern", case, target=pattern)

+                if isinstance(pattern, ast.MatchValue):

+                    self._expression(scope, pattern.value)

+            self._expression(scope, case.guard)

+            self._statements(scope, case.body)

+

+    def _stmt_Import(self, scope, node):

+        for alias in node.names:

+            if alias.asname:

+                self._bind(scope, alias.asname, node.lineno, "import", node, target=alias,

+                           module=alias.name)

+            else:

+

+                       target=node.target)

+        else:

+            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):

+                self._expression(scope, child)

+"""Error-tolerant parsing of Python source into an AST.

+

+Syntax errors are repaired line by line: the offending line is replaced by a

+sequence of progressively more conservative candidates (a placeholder name at

+the cursor, `pass`, and finally a blank line) until the module parses.  Lines

+are never inserted or removed, so AST line numbers match the original file.

+import re

+import time

+# Bindings whose names contain it are ignored by scope analysis.

+_TIME_BUDGET = 1.0

+

+_CLOSERS = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}

+_STATEMENT_KEYWORDS = {

+    "def", "class", "return", "import", "pass", "break", "continue", "raise", "del",

+    "global", "nonlocal", "assert", "while", "with", "try", "except", "finally", "elif",

+}

+# Keywords that, at or below the opening line's indentation, start a new statement.

+_FIRST_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*")

+        elif char in _CLOSERS:

+        elif char in ")]}" and stack and _CLOSERS[stack[-1][0]] == char:

+def strip_comment(line):

+    """Remove a trailing `#` comment, ignoring `#` inside string literals."""

+    quote = None

+    i = 0

+    while i < len(line):

+        char = line[i]

+        if quote:

+            if char == "\\":

+                i += 1

+            elif char == quote:

+                quote = None

+        elif char in "\"'":

+            quote = char

+        elif char == "#":

+            return line[:i]

+        i += 1

+    return line

+def _neighbour_indent(lines):

+    """Indentation of the first code line in `lines`, or None."""

+    for line in lines:

+        if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#"):

+            return len(_indent_of(line))

+    return None

+def _indent_of(line):

+    return line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
